**Access PaySuite picks up Ordo's open banking infrastructure after Neonomics shutdown**

*The acquisition salvages open banking payment initiation and variable recurring payment technology that Neonomics abandoned less than a year after buying the UK fintech.*

Access PaySuite, the payments division of The Access Group, has agreed to acquire Ordo's open banking infrastructure. Ordo built payment initiation and request-to-pay capabilities, and was among the earlier UK fintechs to develop variable recurring payment functionality. Neonomics, the Norwegian open banking firm, acquired Ordo in January 2025 as part of a UK expansion strategy but shut the business down roughly eight months later.

The deal gives Access PaySuite established open banking rails to complement its existing billing and payment collection products, which serve sectors such as housing, utilities and local government. For the broader UK open banking market, the transaction is a small but telling data point: the technology Ordo built retains commercial value even after the company itself failed to survive as an independent entity.

It also underlines a pattern of consolidation among smaller UK open banking firms, where the gap between building viable technology and building a viable business has proved difficult to bridge. Access PaySuite, backed by a larger enterprise software group, is better positioned to absorb the integration costs and find distribution for the product.

*Sources: [Access PaySuite acquires Ordo's open banking technology infrastructure](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47938/access-paysuite-acquires-ordos-open-banking-technology-infrastructure) — Finextra*

**BIS completes Project Aperta to prototype cross-border open finance interoperability**

*The Bank for International Settlements and the UAE central bank have finished a prototype that links open finance networks across jurisdictions, a step towards making domestic data-sharing frameworks work internationally.*

Project Aperta, led by the BIS Innovation Hub and the Central Bank of the UAE, has completed its proof-of-concept phase. The project builds a trusted interoperability layer designed to connect separate national open finance frameworks, allowing cross-border data sharing and financial service delivery without requiring each jurisdiction to adopt identical standards.

The practical problem Aperta addresses is straightforward: open finance regimes are proliferating, but they are being built domestically. A third-party provider authorised in one country cannot easily use its data access rights to serve customers across borders. Aperta's approach creates a network of trust between national frameworks rather than attempting to harmonise them, an architecture that mirrors how cross-border payment systems have typically evolved.

For European observers, the project carries direct relevance. The EU's forthcoming Financial Data Access regulation will establish an open finance framework across the single market, but interconnection with non-EU regimes remains an open question. Aperta offers one model for how that might work, and the UAE's participation signals that Gulf states intend to be early movers in cross-border open finance rather than passive adopters.

*Sources: [CBUAE Completes BIS-Led Project Aperta to Advance Cross-Border Open Finance Interoperability](https://techafricanews.com/2026/06/17/cbuae-completes-bis-led-project-aperta-to-advance-cross-border-open-finance-interoperability/) — TechAfrica News | [UAE Central Bank project could cut delays for firms trading overseas](https://gulfnews.com/business/banking/uae-central-bank-project-could-cut-delays-for-firms-trading-overseas-1.500577128) — Gulf News*

**PayPal shuts down venture capital arm under new CEO's restructuring**

*PayPal is closing its venture unit as CEO Enrique Lores narrows the company's focus amid competitive pressure and reported takeover interest.*

PayPal has confirmed it is winding down its venture capital division, a move that fits a broader pattern of large payment companies pulling back from strategic investing to concentrate on core operations. The decision comes under Enrique Lores, who has been reshaping PayPal since taking the CEO role, with the company facing intensifying competition from Apple Pay, Stripe and buy-now-pay-later providers.

Corporate venture arms in payments have had a mixed record. At their best, they provide early visibility into adjacent technologies and potential acquisition targets. But they also consume management attention and capital that investors increasingly want directed at defending market share. Block scaled back similar activities in 2024; PayPal's move suggests the trend is continuing.

The closure also reflects PayPal's changed strategic posture. The company is reportedly fielding takeover interest, a context in which maintaining a portfolio of minority stakes in startups becomes harder to justify. For the European fintech ecosystem, where PayPal Ventures was an occasional investor, the exit removes one source of late-stage funding at a time when European fintech valuations remain under pressure.

*Sources: [PayPal winds down venture unit](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47945/paypal-winds-down-venture-unit) — Finextra*

**Malta's MFSA sets minimum expectations for PSD3 preparedness**

*The Maltese financial regulator has published specific preparedness requirements for payment service providers and e-money institutions ahead of PSD3 reauthorisation, making it one of the first national authorities to set concrete expectations.*

The Malta Financial Services Authority has published guidance detailing minimum expectations for firms preparing for PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation. The requirements include steps towards reauthorisation, which payment service providers and e-money institutions must complete within 27 months of PSD3's publication in the EU Official Journal.

While the directive and regulation are still moving through the final stages of European adoption, the MFSA's move is notable for its specificity. Most national competent authorities have so far limited their public communications to general awareness-raising. By setting out concrete preparedness steps now, Malta is signalling to its licensed firms — a disproportionate number of which are fintechs and e-money institutions that chose Malta as their EU licensing jurisdiction — that the transition timeline will be enforced actively.

For firms licensed in Malta that passport across the EU, this guidance effectively sets the pace. Other national regulators may follow with their own preparedness frameworks, but the MFSA's early move gives its supervised entities less room to defer planning.

*Sources: [MFSA publishes minimum expectations on PSD3 preparedness](https://www.deloitte.com/mt/en/Industries/banking-capital-markets/perspectives/mfsa-publishes-minimum-expectations-on-psd3-preparedness.html) — Deloitte Malta*

**Stripe and AWS build payment layer for AI agents accessing web content**

*Stripe will power payments within a new AWS Web Application Firewall capability that lets AI agents pay for gated content, extending the emerging infrastructure for autonomous agent commerce.*

Stripe is providing the payments infrastructure for a new AWS capability that enables AI agents to pay for access to web content on behalf of their users. The feature, built into the AWS Web Application Firewall, allows content owners and publishers to gate their material behind a paywall that AI agents can transact against programmatically.

This follows Visa's partnership with OpenAI announced last week and reflects a rapid build-out of the commercial plumbing needed for agentic AI. The difference here is the focus on content rather than consumer purchases: Stripe and AWS are addressing the specific problem of AI agents that need to access paywalled information — research, media, data — as part of completing a task for a user.

For European payment providers, the pattern is becoming clearer. The major US platform and infrastructure companies are moving quickly to define how AI agents will authenticate, authorise and settle payments. The standards and commercial norms being established now will shape whether European payment methods and providers are included in agentic commerce flows or bypassed by them.

*Sources: [Stripe and AWS enable AI agent payments for content owners and publishers](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47940/stripe-and-aws-enable-ai-agent-payments-for-content-owners-and-publishers) — Finextra*
